lesson: In the ERP export, digit-only fields with leading zeros must be formatted as Excel-style formulas (="..."). Standard CSV quoting was tried and rejected because the ERP still strips leading zeros.
why: The ERP importer coerces standard quoted digit strings into numbers, and formula syntax is the only representation it imports byte-for-byte.
quote: A digit-only value with a leading zero has to be written as ="00042" — that's the only thing its parser imports byte-for-byte.

lesson: Do not wrap all export fields in formulas; apply minimal CSV quoting to all other fields, quoting only on commas, quotes, or newlines and doubling embedded quotes.
why: The ERP formula workaround is only required for leading-zero digit strings, whereas standard fields should adhere to standard minimal CSV.
quote: Everything else is normal CSV with minimal quoting: quote a field only if it contains a comma, a quote, or a newline, and double any embedded quotes.

lesson: The CSV export must terminate rows using CRLF (\r\n) line endings instead of bare LF (\n).
why: The ERP parser rejects files formatted with bare newline characters.
quote: And rows must end with \r\n — the ERP parser rejects bare \n line endings.
